title: Evolution of JIT-Enabled Balanced Search Structures in Python: A Historical Simulation from 1960 to 2000
topic: A brief history of just-in-time: forty years of JIT work, from 1960–2000
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
description: We present a deterministic, standard-library-only simulation of the evolution of just-in-time (JIT) compilation techniques from 1960 to 2000, implemented in ...
abstract: We present a deterministic, standard-library-only simulation of the evolution of just-in-time (JIT) compilation techniques from 1960 to 2000, implemented in Python. The core model comprises a minimal bytecode IR, a stack-based interpreter, and a tiered JIT that profiles hot methods, applies peephole optimizations, and emits an optimized bytecode variant. The simulation tracks a balanced search tree that maps JIT milestones to years, preserving strict height-balance and key-ordered invariants. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 64-core processor (1 physical core, 2 logical threads, 7.7~GB RAM, Chronos-Architecture 7.0.0-1017-azure) over 30 iterations yields a mean latency of 108 224.62 \textmu{}s and a throughput of 9 240 ops/s.
